newsitem.title: UK: Green punt to revalue, four others to devalue - HGCA.
newsitem.headline: Green punt to revalue, four others to devalue - HGCA.

text.p: The green rate used for the Irish punt is to be revalued in the European Union's agrimonetary grid on Saturday, the UK Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Friday. Four other green currencies will be devalued on the same day, it added.
The new rate for the Irish punt will be 0.778173 per Ecu compared with the current rate of 0.812908 per Ecu.

The devaluations are for the Belgian franc, which changes to 40.1295 francs from the current 40.0486 francs, the German mark, with a new rate of 1.94738 compared with the current 1.94386, the Dutch guilder, with a new rate of 2.18573 compared with the current 2.18167 and the Austrian schilling, with a new rate of 13.7020, compared with the current 13.6782.
In addition, Sterling enters the fifth and final confirmation period, ahead of a potential revaluation on January 21.
So-called green rates are used by the EU in its Common Agricultural Policy to convert institutional prices, subsidies and levies set in Ecu into national currencies.
